recipes.name: Deep Fried Dill Pickles
ingredients_raw: 1 cup vegetable oil for deep frying

steps.text: In a large bowl, combine 2 eggs, 1/4 cup of the flour, buttermilk, Worcestershire sauce, hot sauce, cayenne pepper, seasoning salt and garlic powder.
In a separate mixing bowl, combine cornmeal, 2 cups flour, salt and 3/4 teaspoon black pepper.
Preheat oil in a deep fryer or pot to 365 degrees F (180 degrees C). Dip drained pickles into milk mixture and then dredge them in the flour mixture.
Drain on paper towels. Salt and pepper to taste

raw_recipe.headline: Deep Fried Dill Pickles
raw_recipe.description: Delicious dill pickles that are battered then fried. This recipe also works well with other pickled vegetables, like pickled peppers.

video.description: See how to batter your dills and fry them to a delicious golden-brown.

review.reviewBody: I've been a fan of these wonderful fried pickles since I serve these at a resturant in Murrells Inlet, SC 17 years ago. I love them best dipped in Dill Dip instead of other salad dressings. I also used flour instead of corn meal.

These are tasty! Make these ahead of time and freeze them...I dip the pickles, then place them on a cookie sheet lined w/wax paper or freezer paper, and put it in the freezer about an hour, then put them in a freezer bag. I use cajun seasoning to make a spicy batch for the adults.

I read some of the comments and decided to try what someone had suggested by combining it all (minus the cornmeal) and using spears instead of chips. It turned out wonderfully, but not as crispy as the pics made it seem. If that doesn't matter to you, go for it, even my mom who openly thinks the whole 'fried pickle' idea is disgusting liked it. We also made fried zucchini (chips or spears work) with this batter, which turned out awesome. Ate it all with a home made rendition of thousand island like someone suggested. Couldn't eat enough!

These were pretty good. I am not a big fan of cornmeal breading, so I halved the cornmeal part, but next time would omit it all together. I prefer a thicker breading for fried pickles and this was more of a thin crunchy textured breading. Which was still good, but just not that perfect coating that I prefer. Otherwise these were yummy and the hubby loved them. Just a little tip if you have extra time beforehand, is to let your pickles release their juice first before breading. Lay your pickles out on several layers of paper towels and lightly salt them to release as much of the pickle juice as possible. Replace with more paper towels as the juice will saturate through. This will help your pickles taste like the restaurant style kind and help them to fry up better with a nice crispness to them. These are great served with ranch for dipping or even a horseradish-ketchup-mayonnaise style of sauce. Thank you for the recipe!

This was my first attempt to make deep fried dills and they were excellent. I used small but whole dill pickles and I spread them out on a paper towel a few hours before to make sure they were dry before hitting the batter. I followed some reviewers suggestions to double batter before frying - I also added some dry mustard powder and garlic powder for just a wee bit more flavour. Next time I might up the cayenne just a tad. Also, I dipped them in Helluva Dill Dip and it was fantastic. This is a keeper!

I used Claussen sandwich slices and cut them into pieces. I followed some other reviews and used half corn meal and half flour, plus I did the double dip method. Mine were super crunchy . I also put all the wet ingredients together and then all the dry. This was good, but I thought batter was a little plain, which maybe was because of the changes I made. All in all, I will make again with some extra spices in the dry mix.

I've been looking for an amazing recipe for fried pickles, and this is definitely one of my top picks. When I made this recipe, I did a couple minor adjustments. First, I omitted the corn meal and combined the wet and dry ingredients to make a batter, rather than dredging the pickles in the flour, for a more even coating. Second, I used pickle spears, because pickle slices tend to get incredibly greasy. If you are going to do a batter, make sure to roll the pickles in a paper towel first to dry them off, to make sure the batter sticks. Also, depending on the moisture in the air, you may want to add additional milk to thin out the batter slightly, so you don't end up with a really thick, rubbery crust. Other than those two changes, I followed the recipe, and the results were out of this world!

Hubs and I make a point to get our deep fried dill pickles every time we’re in Memphis and visit our favorite restaurant/club there. Taking the lead from how they do theirs, I sliced dill pickles myself so that I could get them super thin. Also, I left out the cayenne pepper and hot sauce (Hubs appreciated that) and just added ground black pepper to taste. This is a nice, light batter, nicely seasoned, and using dill pickle slices that are just a little thinner worked out well. Just as our favorite Memphis restaurant does, we served this with a horseradish dipping sauce – I used “Horseradish Dipping Sauce,” recipe also from this site.

Word of caution, this recipe produces an extreme amount of waste from the batter ingredients. You could at least half the wet and dry mixes and still have more than enough to make the entire 32 oz jar of pickles. Definitely use less and don't waste! That being said, I really liked this recipe. Fried pickles are one of my guilty pleasures when eating out. So I went out in search of a recipe to make them at home so I could enjoy them whenever I want. This made a really good crispy coating that doesn't just peel or fall off. Delicious!

Very nice and easy to make. Hubby has been begging me to make these since he had them at a bar. These are very good as is, but after my first batch, I added 1/4 teaspoon of Cajun seasoning to the egg and flour mix. These are a great side for beer or picnic food.

This recipe is by far the BEST that I have tried. If you like a thick crust then double dip in dry and wet. The crust was not at all doughy but very crispy. I did everything exact except I put in more cayenne and season salt in the wet. And I put lots fresh ground pepper to the dry. This recipe made 2 jars of the kosher dill spears. I dipped them in Hidden Valley ranch dressing. Mmmmmm. I added a photo of the finished result.
love it . will be trying it this weekend !!!

What a versatile recipe ! The crunch was perfect, amazing texture. I used some of the batter to deep fry some jalapeño slices and they turned out delicious as well. My guests loved these fritters and the plates were empty before I could come back from the kitchen. The richness of the batter provides such a great balance for the flavors of the briny pickles and the hot peppers. I also add some smoked paprika to the ranch sauce for some extra kick, because why not.
These are amazing! Just like you get in a restaurant but better! I will make again tomorrow for sure! Followed the recipe exactly.

Snow days left me with the opportunity to try something new. This was a great choice!! Makes a big batch if you use the indicated 32 oz. of pickles. I went lightly on the cayenne pepper because of a tummy condition in a family member. Everyone was delighted with the results.

I had tried fried pickles a few times before...once at a southern catered affair and once in a restaurant so I was no stranger to this food. Soooo...I made them as an appetizer for my brother's family birthday party and they were a huge hit....next time I will make a double batch...or should I leave them wanting more?? Side note: I did a panini bar for his birthday and these went well with it.
I liked the flavor of the batter. I found the batter clung to the pickles without any issue. I would make it again, but putting in less cornmeal next time.

Cuddle is right ?? I use this recipe in combination with the editions in Cuddles review, however I go one step further! I grow and make my own pickles, I make them the Jewish style way that most people would relate to the Batamphe recipe of half sours, and those of you that like that crispy half sour type of pickle I have an excellent recipe that you can use just by picking up some pickling cukes at your local farmers market or grocery store! Once they have been pickled to perfection (which only takes less than a week, roughly 5 days) if you combine these with this recipe with Cuddles additions? You have an appetizer your guests will be BEGGING to learn!! Ask if you would like my pickling recipe(s), I have all different types that I make, spicy, sweet, dill, half sour, old bay, etc!!

These are excellent. I cut the recipe in 1/2 and didn't really measure the pickles. I made them for College Football Saturday and they were a hit with my hubs. We've had them at restaurants but he said these were even better. This will be my go to recipe and as the author says, you can really use this recipe for any kind of veggie you want. Thank you for posting your recipe Marbalet.
